title: Anthropic polled 1,334 of its employees. They're more sure than most of us that AI will take over jobs.
source_used: Anthropic research page 'The AI expectations gap' (full text) and Business Insider (full text)
key_facts: August 2026 surveys of a nationally representative sample of US adults and of Anthropic staff; Business Insider says 1,334 Anthropic employees were polled.
Over half of Anthropic staff expect AI to do at least 80% of their current work by 2030, versus 5% of US workers.
On average staff expect AI to do 75% of their current work by 2030, versus 28% for US workers.
91% of staff and 39% of US adults expect AI to make a Nobel-level discovery by 2030.

Workers in manual trades, production and transport expect AI to do the least of their work (Business Insider); the median Anthropic staff member expects AI to do 95% of the work of building a new AI model by end of 2030.
Model-implied 2030 GDP growth from the median answers is 5.4% for US adults and 17.1% for staff; these are derived figures, not stated forecasts.
Peter McCrory, Anthropic's chief economist, said Anthropic runs roughly a year and a half ahead of the economy on AI adoption (Business Insider).
quote_evidence: When it comes to their own job, over half of Anthropic staff expect AI to be able to do at least 80% of their current work by 2030, compared with 5% of US workers.
The median Anthropic employee said that by the end of 2030, they expect AI to handle 95% of the work of building a new AI model.
These are the personal expectations of staff members in an internal poll and do not represent Anthropic's plans or its view of its headcount.
why_it_matters_hint: Staff at a leading AI lab expect far more automation of their own work than ordinary US workers do.
notes: Company's own survey research; opinions, not outcomes.
